st.headline: Sheng Siong shares continue last week’s slide, fall over 9% to hit one-year low
st.teaser: The company says competition in grocery retail could intensify over the coming year.
fullText: SINGAPORE - Shares of supermarket operator Sheng Siong continued to fall, dropping as much as 9.4 per cent on the morning of Nov 2, after the group reported a marginal 1.9 per cent year-on-year increase in third-quarter net profit on the evening of Oct 29.
The stock had closed down 4.6 per cent or S$0.13 at S$2.67 on Oct 30.
The counter opened on Nov 2 down 7.1 per cent at S$2.48 as at 9.01am, before slipping to S$2.46 as at 9.16 am.
It fell further to S$2.42, down 9.4 per cent, as at 10.44am. This is the lowest level the stock has reached since Nov 3, 2025, when it hit S$2.33 in intra-day trade.
Some 7.4 million shares changed hands as at 10.44am on Nov 2. No married deals were reported, according to data from ShareInvestor.
The mainboard-listed supermarket operator reported a net profit of S$44.6 million for the three months ended Sept 30, up from S$43.7 million in the corresponding year-ago period.

Revenue for the quarter rose 6.2 per cent to S$441.5 million, from S$415.5 million a year earlier. The group attributed the increase to a larger store network in Singapore, as well as improvements in comparable same-store sales.

The stock’s decline also comes after management said during its Q3 results briefing that the grocery retail landscape remains competitive, with sustained promotional activity potentially putting pressure on revenue and margins.

Competition could intensify further with the upcoming Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link, which is expected to begin operations in February 2027. The link could encourage more cross-border shopping and heighten price competition for selected packaged groceries and household products.
Sheng Siong said it would adapt its strategies as developments surrounding the RTS Link unfold, in order to address the potential impact on its business.

Beyond competition, the group also flagged rising labour costs as another challenge. These include wage increases under the Progressive Wage Model and the National Wages Council’s guidelines for 2026 to 2027.
The group had raised the salaries of its retail workers in September last year to meet Progressive Wage Model requirements for the retail sector.

DBS analyst Chee Zheng Feng said in a note on Friday that he expects Sheng Siong’s earnings growth to moderate further in the fourth quarter, as it comes down from a high base boosted by SG60 vouchers.

Another potential factor is the full-quarter impact of the Thomson Imperial Court store’s closure on Sep 25, while higher utility prices and rising staff costs could also weigh on the supermarket chain’s profitability, he added.
The brokerage maintained a hold and unchanged target price of S$3 for the counter. THE BUSINESS TIMES

cna.headline: BOJ flags progress in anchoring inflation around target
cna.teaser: BOJ flags progress in anchoring inflation around target
fullText: TOKYO, Nov 2 : Japan has made gradual progress towards anchoring inflation around the central bank's 2 per cent target, the Bank of Japan said in a report on Monday, bolstering the case for raising interest rates.

In reaching its decision, the BOJ weighed up inflation expectations, firms' wage- and price-setting behaviour, and the degree to which households and firms act based on the assumption that prices will rise by around 2 per cent, the central bank said.

"With underlying inflation moving around 2 per cent and upside risks to prices warranting attention, interest rate hikes will likely alleviate price pressures and underpin consumption," the bank said in the full version of its quarterly outlook.
Firms' inflation outlook appears to gradually converge around 2 per cent, while households' inflation expectations vary widely, it added.
"As such, underlying inflation has risen toward a level around 2 per cent over the past few years, and there has been gradual progress toward anchoring it at that level."
Domestic consumption has recently been sluggish in real terms, the bank added, due to bad weather during the summer and a hit to spending from rising living costs.
"But consumption as a whole is likely to remain resilient" partly thanks to government subsidies to curb fuel prices, higher stock prices and rising wages from a tight job market, it said.
The BOJ publishes the full version of its quarterly report on the market day after it concludes its policy meeting, at which it releases a summary.

economistArticle.title: The Parenting Trap: Why Hard Work by Less-Affluent Parents Cannot Bridge the Class Gap
paras: Over the past few decades, the ethos of intensive parenting—spending vast amounts of time, energy, and money on stimulating children's cognitive growth—has ceased to be an exclusive practice of the wealthy elite. Working-class and lower-middle-class parents now read to their infants, enroll them in extracurricular activities, and carefully monitor their homework with a dedication that rivals their wealthier peers.

This shift reflects a widespread anxiety about social mobility in an increasingly competitive economy. Parents across all income brackets recognize that educational achievement is paramount for securing stable employment. Consequently, even families operating on modest budgets sacrifice leisure hours and disposable income to purchase educational toys, private tutoring, and sports coaching.

Yet, despite this democratization of effort, the developmental gap between children of different socio-economic strata persists. Richer parents possess financial reserves that enable them to buy structural advantages—such as elite private schooling, specialized exam preparation, and broad international exposure—that low-income parents simply cannot replicate regardless of their dedication.

Moreover, prosperous parents command significant social capital. They can secure prestigious internships through professional networks and navigate complex educational systems with ease. This implicit leverage transforms high effort into tangible career rewards far more reliably than effort alone can achieve for less-connected families.

Thus, while intensive parenting has become a universal norm, it has not proven to be the great equalizer many hoped for. Policy interventions must move beyond simply urging parents to work harder, focusing instead on structural remedies like subsidizing high-quality early childhood care and broadening access to top-tier educational pathways.
economistArticle.cn:
在过去的几十年里，“密集型育儿”的理念——即投入大量时间、精力和金钱来刺激儿童的认知成长——已不再是富裕精英阶层的专属做法。工薪阶层和中产阶级下层的父母现在也像富裕同行一样，热衷于为婴儿朗读、报名参加课外活动，并仔细监督孩子的作业。

这种转变反映了人们在竞争日益激烈的经济环境中对社会阶层流动性的普遍焦虑。各个收入阶层的父母都认识到，教育成就对于获得稳定就业至关重要。因此，即便预算紧张的家庭也会牺牲休闲时间和可支配收入，去购买教育玩具、请私人补习和参加体育教练课程。

然而，尽管这种努力走向了普及，不同社会经济阶层儿童之间的发展差距依然存在。富裕父母拥有雄厚的财务储备，使其能够购买结构性优势——例如精英私立教育、专业考试辅导以及广泛的国际视野——而无论低收入父母多么投入，都根本无法复制这些优势。

此外，富裕父母拥有丰厚的社会资本。他们能通过职业网络为子女争取到名企实习机会，并从容应对复杂的教育体系。相比人脉较少的家庭，这种隐性优势能更稳定地将高额投入转化为实在的职业回报。

因此，尽管密集型育儿已成为一种普遍规范，但事实证明它并非人们所期待的社会平等调节器。政策干预必须超越单纯呼吁父母更加努力，转而关注结构性补救措施，例如补贴高质量的早期托育服务以及拓宽通往顶尖教育资源的途径。

gems.s: This shift reflects a widespread anxiety about social mobility in an increasingly competitive economy.
gems.why: This sentence uses concise abstract nouns ('shift', 'anxiety', 'mobility') to succinctly link behavioral change with macro-economic pressure. 句子通过使用抽象名词（转变、焦虑、流动性），将微观行为与宏观经济压力有机联系在一起。

gems.s: Thus, while intensive parenting has become a universal norm, it has not proven to be the great equalizer many hoped for.
gems.why: The contrast clause starting with 'while' effectively sets up a concession before delivering a critical conclusion using the metaphor 'great equalizer'. 使用 while 引导的让步状语从句，随后用“伟大平衡器”这一比喻引出深刻的结论。
